- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment surges.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for 2–3 periods post-spike.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price in early periods when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is trending up.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., +0.4, -0.2, +0.6), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
